pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values | Cherhill C of E (VA) Primary School
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Vision and Values
Our Vision
Our vision for Cherhill C. of E. Primary School is to provide a caring, creative, Christian community where everyone will achieve with confidence and enjoyment. We will nurture growth and development in all aspects of school life so that everyone will enjoy:
‘Life in all its fullness.’ The Gospel of John.
Our School Values
As a Christian School Community we embody the following values:
hristian school focused on our wider community
A belief that our Christian values should underpin all our work and relationships with the community
appiness and imagination
A belief in the importance of ensuring a happy environment for all in which imagination can flourish
mpathy and Respect for All
A belief that empathy with, and respect for all members of the school community is essential in a Christian school
eflection and Aspiration
A belief that time for reflection is essential for both children and staff in order to sustain high aspiration
onesty and Care
A belief that honesty and care for others are essential in our relationships with each other
nnovation and Motivation
A belief in and commitment to innovation to sustain high levels of motivation
A belief that as a Christian school Christian love and faith inform all we do
earning Community
Together these values help us to develop as a learning community
Church Links
As a Church of England School we have close links with St James' church in Cherhill. We attend the church for special services throughout the year such as Harvest, Christmas, Easter and a special service for our Year 6 leavers.
The Rev Matt Earwicker, rector, and Mrs Pam Evans, lay preacher, help the school by taking collective worship on a Tuesday morning.
For more information about the church and the Oldbury Benefice please visit https://www.oldburybenefice.org.uk/
Spirituality
At Cherhill Primary School we value the spiritual development of our children and have agreed the following definition to define spiritual development:
The spiritual development of pupils is shown by their:
willingness to reflect on their experiences.

pageCache.text:
Before & Afterschool Club
Breakfast and Afterschool Club
We are pleased to offer high-quality wraparound care at Cherhill Primary School in partnership with PH ActiveEd. Our Breakfast and After-School Clubs give children a safe, welcoming environment before and after the school day. Every session is fully organised and delivered by PH ActiveEd's own staff, using their own resources, so there is nothing for families to arrange beyond booking a place.
Safe, registered and trusted
PH ActiveEd is an Ofsted-registered childcare provider. All staff hold an enhanced DBS, paediatric first aid and safeguarding training as a minimum, and each setting has its own risk assessment in place. Because PH ActiveEd is Ofsted registered, you can pay using Tax-Free Childcare and childcare vouchers, as well as by card.
In the mornings, Breakfast Club offers a calm start, with a healthy breakfast, time with friends and quiet activities to ease into the day, so children feel settled and ready for a positive start to learning.
After school, children enjoy a wider mix, from outdoor play and physical activity to more relaxed options such as Lego, games and arts and crafts, giving them the chance to unwind, be active and choose how to end their day.
7:30am - 8:30am: £6.20
3:00 - 4:00pm: £6.30
3:00 - 5:30pm: £12.90*
4:00 - 5:30pm: £8.95*
*includes a healthy, light snack
Bookings for September are made through PH ActiveEd's new online booking system. To register and book a place, visit:
https://bookings.phactiveed.co.uk/
This is a new booking page, so if you have not used it before you will need to re-register, even if you had an account previously. When you register, please follow all the on-screen instructions. Once registered, you can log back in at any time to make bookings.
For more information on childcare vouchers, Tax-Free Childcare, FAQs and policies, please visit https://phactiveed.co.uk/ and go to the For Parents tab or go to: https://phactiveed.co.uk/pages/childcare-vouchers

pageCache.pageTitle: New Reception Information - Starting School | Cherhill C of E (VA) Primary School
pageCache.text:
New Reception Information - Starting School
In February 2024 we had an Ofsted inspection where the school was rated as good. Early Years provision at our school was rated as outstanding.
Below are a few quotes about the Early Years from our report:
Children in Reception get off to an excellent start. Well-trained staff support children’s language development exceptionally well. Staff create purposeful opportunities to develop children’s speech and vocabulary. Children learn to read from the moment they start school.
The early years provision in this school is exceptional. Children learn the routines and habits of school from the very beginning. Children are highly motivated and eager to join in.
Pupils’ conduct is exemplary. This starts in Reception, where children learn how to develop friendships as they play together and share.
At Cherhill we know that the Reception Year is so incredibly important, and we are here to support you and your child every step of the way.
We will be having our Open Mornings on Thursday 1st October 9:00 - 12:00 and Thursday 5th November 9:00 - 12:00. Please see the flyer attached below.
If you have any questions please feel free to contact the office on 01249 812100 or email office@cherhill.wilts.sch.uk
Please do take a look at the Emerald Class Page on this website as it will show you some of the exciting ways we learn in Reception.
Reception Teacher and Deputy Head

pageCache.pageTitle: Anti Bullying Ambassadors | Cherhill C of E (VA) Primary School
pageCache.text:
Anti Bullying Ambassadors
Children
Anti Bullying Ambassadors
Anti Bullying Week 2023
Anti Bullying Week 2023
Anti-Bullying Ambassadors at Cherhill school 2023
Anti-Bullying Week 2022 at Cherhill
The theme for this year was 'Reach Out' and aimed to encourage children to reach out if they think they might be experiencing bullying. We started the week off by wearing odd socks to show that we are all unique. With support, the Y6 Anti-Bullying ambassadors planned and delivered an assembly to the whole school to introduce the theme of the week and to invite Y5 children to join them as Anti-Bullying Ambassadors for the next year. They wrote a letter of application expressing why they should be chosen to fulfil the role. The pupils also wear blue bibs on the playground so that they are easily recognised by other pupils who might need their support.
Each class discussed bullying with their teachers throughout the week and completed activities that reminded them of ways that they can reach out for help if they are being bullied.
